heard: Astronauts in orbit cannot see the Great Wall of China. From 400 kilometers up on the space station, city lights glow brightly at night. By day, astronauts easily spot the pyramids of Giza and the 2.3-kilometer Three Gorges Dam. But the Great Wall's widest sections measure only about 9 to 10 meters across. At that altitude, it is roughly 10 times narrower than the human eye's one-arc minute resolving limit. Because it was built from local dirt and stone, it blends into the rugged mountains. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, confirmed he could not spot it at all. Astronaut Lirei Chao photographed sections through a telephoto lens, but his naked eye saw nothing. A 1754 legend claimed it was visible from the moon, but orbital reality proved far different.
differences: 'leroy chiao' heard as 'lirei chao' after 'at all astronaut'
